Beholding them, the son of Ravana, addressing those rangers of

seven and nine monkeys at one time to the great delight of the 
titans. Thereafter that invincible warrior crushed those 
monkeys under his shafts that glittered like the sun and were 
decorated with gold. 
Their limbs pierced, the monkeys, overwhelmed by those

this second Aditya who consumed them with those formidable

brief.summary_1line: Indrajit performs rituals, becomes invisible using divine power, and devastates the monkey army with a rain of arrows, wounding many leaders including Rama and Lakshmana.

image_candidates.scene_text: Indrajit performs a fiery sacrificial ritual before battle, flames swirling as he seizes a goat and invokes the gods beside his war chariot.
Invisible in the sky, Indrajit rains blazing arrows down on the monkey army as warriors fall amid shattered trees and rocks.
The monkey heroes—Hanuman, Sugriva, Angada, and others—stand bloodied under a storm of arrows while the unseen Indrajit attacks from the heavens.

deep.rich_summary: After heavy Rakshasa losses, the survivors report to Ravana that many of his champions—including Devantaka, Trishiras, and Atikaya—have been slain. Ravana sinks into grief, but his formidable son Indrajita vows to avenge them and destroy Rama and Lakshmana. He departs in a magnificent war chariot accompanied by monstrous Rakshasa forces mounted on strange beasts. Before battle he performs a dark sacrificial rite to the fire god, invoking cosmic powers and the Brahma weapon. Empowered by the ritual, Indrajita becomes invisible in the sky. From this unseen vantage he unleashes a devastating storm of enchanted arrows on the monkey army, striking down their greatest leaders and spreading panic across the battlefield. Even Rama recognizes the divine power behind Indrajita’s invisibility and prepares to endure the assault, allowing the demon prince to believe he has achieved victory.

highlight_spans.why: Marks the beginning of the battle episode within the Yuddha Kanda, where the war escalates with Indrajita’s intervention.
Indrajita reassures his grieving father and vows to strike down Rama and Lakshmana, revealing both filial loyalty and terrifying confidence.
The sacrificial ritual to the fire god and invocation of cosmic powers—this moment explains the supernatural source of Indrajita’s battlefield advantage.
Indrajita disappears into the sky through magical power, a pivotal turning point that allows him to wage invisible warfare.
The monkey heroes are struck down in waves by Indrajita’s enchanted arrows, emphasizing the scale of devastation and the despair spreading through Rama’s army.

top_scenes.scene_text: Indrajita performing a blazing sacrificial ritual before battle, offering a goat into smokeless golden fire while Rakshasa warriors and monstrous mounts gather around.
The invisible Indrajita in the sky raining glowing arrows like a storm onto the monkey army below as giants like Hanuman, Sugriva, and Angada are struck amid chaos.
Rama and Lakshmana standing amid a devastated battlefield, calmly enduring the unseen assault while arrows fall around them and wounded monkey warriors lie scattered.
